1.
This is claim petition filed u/s 166/140 of M.V. Act.

As per the averments of the claim petition,
deceased Radhika Devi died in a roadside accident occurred on 17.10.2014.
It is stated that on 17.10.2014 at about 06:30 PM deceased Radhika Devi along with her friend Manju Srivastav were standing at G.T. Road, Mohan Nagar towards Delhi and waiting for TSR.

In the meantime, one Tempo bearing registration no.DL-1PL-3299 which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, violating all traffic rules hit the deceased Radhika Devi resultantly, deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
After the accident she was taken to Ambey Hospital, Ghaziabad where she succumbed to accidental injuries.
2. It is mentioned in the claim petition that regarding the accident in question, FIR no. 1315/2014 under Section 279/338/304-A IPC was registered at PS Sahibabad, Distt. Ghaziabad.

It is stated that at the time of MACT No.1229/2016 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER Page 2 MALIK Date:
2024.04.10 16:24:06 +0530 death deceased was aged around 58 years and was self employed as doing tailoring/stitching work and earning around Rs. 12,000/- to Rs. 15,000/- per month.
It is stated that petitioners being husband, children were dependent.
3. Perusal of the record shows that after filing of the claim petition, respondent no. 1 was proceeded ex parte on 15.11.2016.
Said order was however recalled on the application of the respondent on 18.07.2017.
Respondent no. 1 filed the WS taking an objection that claim petition is without any cause of action.

It is pleaded that on 17.10.2014 respondent no. 1 was going by commercial vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1PL-3299 towards Delhi and when he reached at Main G.T. Road,
Mohan Nagar, he saw 10-15 persons gathered who made protest against the police.
Due to that protest, traffic was moving very slow.

Police official raised signal to stop the vehicle, respondent no.
1 stated to have stopped his vehicle and inquired from said police officials.
It is stated that police officials directed respondent no. 1 to come to the police station.
One Constable stated to have accompanied respondent no. 1 to PS where it is pleaded that, in connivance of the relatives of the deceased, respondent no. 1 was implicated in the accident case.
It is pleaded that driver was holding valid DL.
Other averments of the claim petition have been denied.
4. Respondent no. 2/owner was also proceeded ex-parte when he did not appear despite being served by way of publication vide order dated 04.09.2018.

(iv) Fabricated policy mentioned serial number containing 9 Digit whereas under the Genisys system, there used to be 8 Digit serial number of the policy.

Issue No.1 10.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of MACT No.1229/2016 SHAILENDER Page 5 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 16:24:31 +0530 evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012),
Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530,
Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: In the present case, only witness examined on behalf of petitioner is PW-1 Lallan Singh who is admittedly not an eye witness.
However, in the evidence of PW-1 has proved certified copy of criminal case Ex. PW-1/12.
As a matter of record respondent no. 1/driver of the offending vehicle has been prosecuted in FIR No. 1315/2014 of PS Sahibabad in respect of accident in question.

Certified copy of criminal case documents like Report under Section 173 Cr.PC, FIR, compliant,
mechanical inspection report, site plan etc. clearly establish by preponderance of probabilities that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1 while driving offending vehicle no. DL-1PL-3299.
12.
No doubt in the pleadings, respondent no. 1 has taken the plea of being falsely implicated by the police in the present case when he was passing through the Main G.T. Road.
However, respondent no. 1 after filing the WS, stopped appearing in the proceedings and did not lead any evidence nor examined himself in this regard.

Another important aspect to note in this context is that if according to respondent no. 1, he was falsely implicated in the accident in question by the local police, no complaint or representation has been filed by respondent no. 1 at any Legal Forum.

As such, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material available on record MACT No.1229/2016 Digitally signed by SHAILENDER Page 6 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 16:24:38 +0530 which establish atleast by preponderance of probabilities that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1, resulting into death of the deceased.
Issue stands decided in favour of the petitioner.

4 13.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 14.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Smt. Radhika Devi.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier) Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.

Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with MACT No.1229/2016 Digitally signed by SHAILENDER Page 8 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 16:24:54 +0530 reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

LIABILITY 28.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Insurance company in this case has taken the plea of fake insurance policy.
In para 3 of the WS of respondent no.3/ insurance, different reasons have been given for establishing that insurance policy as relied upon in respect of offending vehicle was fake.

On behalf of respondent no.3 witness R3W1 Praveen Gupta, Deputy Manager of R3 has been examined who in his deposition has testified that respondent no.3/insurance company has checked the particulars of purported insurance policy no.091895/31/11/4/000005360, same has never been issued by the respondent no.3.
Witness states that said policy is fake because respondent no.3/insurance company has computerized policy issuing system.

Prior thereto it used Genisys system, by which policy number was prepared in following sequence : (A) Six digits of office code; (B) two digits of department code; (C) two digits of year of policy; (D) followed by code of either 01 for package policy or 02 for liability only policy and ;
(E) 08 digit MACT No.1229/2016 SHAILENDER MALIK Page 14 MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 16:25:43 +0530 serial number of policy.

29. Witness states that in the present case the purported policy is fabricated because policy is shown to have been issued from office of Indra Palace, (Behind Plaza Cinema), Connaught Place and office code has been mentioned is 091895 whereas the correct office code of that office is 041701.
PW R3W1 further says that year of the policy has been mentioned as 11 whereas it has been issued for period of 03.03.2014 to 02.03.2015, therefore the correct code for year was 14 instead of 11.
Witness further says that in fabricated policy instead of mentioning 01 or 02 for category of policy, category code has been mentioned as 4 which is incorrect.
30. PW R3W1 further testifies that in the policy in question number of digits of policy number are nine, whereas the numbers of digits of genuine policy issued under Genesis system are to be eight.

Witness further says that signatures at the bottom of the policy by mere two lines joint at the spot clearly show that the policy was forged and fabricated as no name or designation of signatory has been mentioned.
Witness further proved the sample policy as generally issued by the respondent no.3/ insurance company as Ex.R3W1/3.

Witness further proved service of notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC upon driver, owner of the offending vehicle no.DL-1PL-3299 and stated that they did not respond to that notice despite service of the same.

sentences.text: Having considered the evidence and examining the submissions made at bar, first of all it be noted that evidence of R3W1 was essentially regarding fake policy of offending vehicle no.DL-1PL-3299 , as such evidence was against respondent no.1 and 2 (driver and owner) of said vehicle, however these respondents did not cross examine that witness at all.
Even in the cross examination of R3W1 by counsel for the petitioner nothing substantive has come on the record.
No suggestion has been given to the witness that the grounds on the basis of which witness R3W1 tried to prove the policy being fake, are incorrect.

In the absence of any such suggestion and nothing substantive come in the cross examination, this Tribunal finds that witness has clearly given specific and cogent reasons duly supported with sample insurance policy generally issued by respondent no.3 company.
In such circumstance this Tribunal finds that insurance company has proved by preponderance of probability that insurance policy of offending vehicle as relied upon being fake.
34. No doubt regarding the claim of insurance company policy being fake, no separate complaint has been filed by respondent no.3 company.
However filing of complaint to policy authority is just a ritual, when otherwise the fact of insurance policy being fake is proved by other evidence which remained uncontroverted.

The judgment of Gauhati High Court in Darilian Passah's case (supra) is also based on same logics MACT No.1229/2016 Digitally signed by Page 16 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 16:26:05 +0530 wherein it is stated that when insurance company has prima facie shown that serial number of the policy did not tally with the number of insurance policy being issued during relevant year, that fact stand proved by preponderance of probability.
Similar is the ratio of judgment of Bombay and Jharkhand High Courts as relied upon counsel for insurance.
Thus this Tribunal finds that R3 has proved the insurance policy relied upon is fake.

In this case no directions can be given to the insurance company for making the payment of compensation amount and then to recover from respondent no.1 and 2 because there was no contractual liability of respondent no.3/insruance company at all to pay the compensation when the insurance policy in itself is a fake and does not impose any binding duty to reimburse the amount of compensation by respondent no.3.
As such the liability to pay compensation is upon respondent no.1 and 2 being jointly and severally liable.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of pleadings as come on the record ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 04.09.2018 framed following issues :
(1)Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 17.10.2014 at about 06:30 PM at G.T Road, from Mohan Nagar to Delhi, PS Sahibabad, Ghaziabad,
U.P due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle no. DL-1PL-3299 being driven by Lallan Singh vs Juned Akhter on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83588588/
3
respondent no. 1/driver?
OPP (2)Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of MACT No.1229/2016 SHAILENDER Page 5 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 16:24:31 +0530 evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012),
Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530,
Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.
Certified copy of criminal case documents like Report under Section 173 Cr.PC, FIR, compliant,
mechanical inspection report, site plan etc. clearly establish by preponderance of probabilities that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1 while driving offending vehicle no. DL-1PL-3299.
12.
However, respondent no. 1 after filing the WS, stopped appearing in the proceedings and did not lead any evidence nor examined himself in this regard.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Smt. Radhika Devi.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the MACT No.1229/2016 SHAILENDER MALIK Page 7 MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 16:24:46 +0530 case of death:
(a) age of the deceased;
(b) income of the deceased; and (c) the number of dependents.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Lallan Singh vs Juned Akhter on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83588588/
5 Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier) Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with MACT No.1229/2016 Digitally signed by SHAILENDER Page 8 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.04.10 16:24:54 +0530 reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
Therefore,
in the absence of any evidence, notional income of deceased is to be determined.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
 Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)
23.
Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.
In such circumstance this Tribunal finds that insurance company has proved by preponderance of probability that insurance policy of offending vehicle as relied upon being fake.
However filing of complaint to policy authority is just a ritual, when otherwise the fact of insurance policy being fake is proved by other evidence which remained uncontroverted.
Thus this Tribunal finds that R3 has proved the insurance policy relied upon is fake.
In this case no directions can be given to the insurance company for making the payment of compensation amount and then to recover from respondent no.1 and 2 because there was no contractual liability of respondent no.3/insruance company at all to pay the compensation when the insurance policy in itself is a fake and does not impose any binding duty to reimburse the amount of compensation by respondent no.3.
